hypothesis: The training batch had one failure (mqx-071), out of 20 cases. That's too little evidence to prove a pattern, but it shows a general weakness. The doctor trusted the patient's lay self-report ("my hearing hasn't changed") over an objective exam finding (bilateral decreased hearing). It used three exam requests asking the record for HINTS details that weren't there instead of ordering the test that would settle the question (audiometry). It then submitted a closely related diagnosis (vestibular neuritis) that the abnormal finding ruled out, and listed the conflict as an unresolved 'gap'. USMLE-style vignettes often hinge on a single objective feature that separates two related diagnoses, so the doctor should treat exam and test results as ground truth. It should run a pre-submission check that the chosen diagnosis explains every abnormal finding. When a conflict remains, it should spend a request on the test that settles it rather than re-asking for missing record details.
changes: harness/system.md: added a 'How to weigh evidence' section. Objective findings outrank what the patient says; don't keep re-requesting details the record lacks; when the top two diagnoses differ by one feature, order the test for that feature. Also added a 3-step pre-submit checklist: list the abnormal findings, check the diagnosis explains all of them (otherwise switch to the related diagnosis or resolve the conflict), and give the most specific fitting diagnosis.

harness/lessons.md: added two general lessons. Don't let a patient's denial override an exam finding; this one uses neuritis vs labyrinthitis and cholecystitis vs cholangitis as examples of close pairs decided by one finding. And spend requests on new discriminating tests rather than repeating requests the record can't answer.
expected_effect: This should fix cases where the doctor picks a related diagnosis while ignoring or explaining away a recorded abnormality. Examples are neuritis vs labyrinthitis and other close pairs decided by one finding. It should also reduce wasted exam requests. I expect a small gain on held-out cases, with little risk to cases that already pass, because the change only adds a consistency check before submission and leaves the interview length unchanged. The prompt files total about 2.5k characters, well under the 16,000 limit.
